evals.prompt: Our standard-risk production agent has no governance at all yet. Set it up from scratch: risk classification, policy, enforcement, and audit.
evals.expected_behavior: Follows the documented workflow order: classifies the risk level first, then defines a GovernancePolicy (allowed tools, blocked patterns, rate limits), then enforces at the tool boundary with @govern or framework-equivalent middleware, then wires audit logging — not enforcement code written before a policy exists.
assertions: Classifies a governance level (open/standard/strict/locked) before writing any policy or enforcement code
Defines a GovernancePolicy object before wiring the enforcement decorator
Adds enforcement at the tool boundary rather than scattering checks inside business logic
Wires audit logging for allowed, denied, and error events only after policy and enforcement exist

evals.prompt: Add tool allowlists, rate limits, and append-only audit logs to this production coding agent that calls external APIs.
evals.expected_behavior: Chooses a governance level from risk, defines a policy with allowed tools and limits, enforces at the tool boundary, and wires audit events for allowed, denied, and error outcomes with fail-closed behavior.
assertions: Defines a governance policy with allowed tools or blocked patterns
Enforces controls at the tool boundary rather than only documenting them
Includes audit trail or logging of allowed and denied events
Mentions fail-closed behavior when governance checks error

evals.prompt: We have multiple agents that can call privileged tools. Add trust scoring and human approval for sensitive operations.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds multi-agent trust scoring before privileged access and requires human approval for sensitive tools without mixing in supply-chain integrity manifests.
assertions: Mentions trust scoring or multi-agent privilege gating
Mentions human approval for sensitive tool operations
Stays focused on runtime governance rather than package integrity hashing

evals.prompt: Our agent already has a working GovernancePolicy (allowed_tools defined, @govern applied, audit trail wired). We just need a max_calls_per_request rate limit added on top. Don't touch anything else.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds the rate-limit field/check to the existing policy and enforcement path without redefining the already-working allowlist, re-adding the @govern decorator elsewhere, rewriting the audit trail, or introducing trust scoring/intent classification that was not asked for.
assertions: Scopes the change to the rate-limit control only
Does not rewrite or restate the already-working allowlist or audit trail implementation
Does not add trust scoring, intent classification, or human-approval flows that were not requested
Confirms the rate limit denies at the configured threshold rather than only documenting the field

evals.prompt: Generate a SHA-256 manifest for this plugin and gate promotion on integrity verification.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from agent-governance because the task is supply-chain integrity, not runtime tool policy.
assertions: Does not implement runtime tool allowlists for a manifest/integrity request
Routes toward agent-supply-chain or integrity-manifest work instead
